claims.text: Catalytic performance in transition-metal catalysts is governed by the energetic position of the d-band center.
Surface strain can modulate the energetic position of the d-band center.
Increasing tensile strain shifts the d-band center upward.
An upward shift of the d-band center optimizes the adsorption energies of key reaction intermediates.
Optimized intermediate adsorption energies enhance catalytic activity, selectivity, or durability.
A pre-strained or flexible support can transfer tensile stress to the surface of metal nanoparticles.
Tensile strain alters the surface atomic arrangement.
The strain-altered surface atomic arrangement causes a measurable shift in the d-band center relative to the Fermi level.
Tensile-strain-induced d-band modulation lowers activation-energy barriers for key reaction steps.
Strain-induced electronic changes can reduce poisoning or deactivation processes.
The strained catalyst will exhibit a higher turnover frequency and/or improved selectivity than the unstrained baseline.
The strained catalyst will exhibit better long-term stability than the unstrained baseline.
Performance improvement will correlate with an upward shift in the measured d-band center.
The proposed relationship is limited to comparable particle sizes and morphologies for which strain can be reliably imparted.
The magnitude of d-band-center shift required for significant performance improvement may depend on reaction conditions and catalyst-support interactions.
